summary: A 14-day analysis of Nightscout telemetry and AAPS settings reveals an 86.0% time-in-range, an 8.9% time above range, and a 5.1% time below range. The user relies entirely on UAM-driven closed-loop automation without explicit manual carb logging. This creates a reactive pattern with afternoon post-prandial spikes followed by delayed insulin accumulation and late hypoglycemia.

analysis_steps.findings: Data stream is complete and reliable for closed-loop telemetry audit, with 98.7% CGM coverage and valid device statuses and treatments.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3,995 valid raw CGM entries; 6,214 device statuses; 2,315 treatments over 14 days.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Absence of explicit manual carb entries prevents a standard post-prandial CR evaluation.

analysis_steps.findings: Time below range of 5.1% exceeds the 4% safety threshold, driven by nocturnal dipping and post-correction insulin stacking.
analysis_steps.evidence: Time in range 86.0%, time above range 8.9%, time below range 5.1% with glucose extremes down to 41-42 mg/dL.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight basal rates show mild dipping below 70 mg/dL while afternoon segments experience persistent hyperglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: Overnight average glucose 90-106 mg/dL with 10-18% time below range; afternoon local hour 16 average 162.8 mg/dL with up to 32% time above range.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of declared meals makes it difficult to separate basal insufficiency from unannounced nutritional intake during afternoon highs.

analysis_steps.findings: A 10-hour DIA combined with frequent SMB dosing and flat ISF profile creates overlapping automation and stacking risks.
analysis_steps.evidence: Profile DIA set to 10 hours; flat ISF at 56 mg/dL/U; mixed correction responses in telemetry windows.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Interaction between long DIA and oref1 closed-loop calculations requires careful observation.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are fully active with SMB always enabled, successfully catching unannounced rises but increasing IOB accumulation.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled=true, uam_enabled=true, smb_always_enabled=true with active microbolusing observed in loop traces.

analysis_steps.findings: Dynamic ISF at 70% is active and compensating for profile rigidity, supported by broad safety limits.
analysis_steps.evidence: autosens_enabled=false, dynamic_sensitivity_enabled=true, adjustment factor 70%, max basal 12 U/h, max IOB 25 U.

analysis_steps.findings: Absence of manual meal announcements forces a reactive UAM response, causing post-prandial spikes followed by delayed automated correction.
analysis_steps.evidence: carb_entries=0 and therapy response windows show no manual preboluses.

analysis_steps.findings: Extended carb features are not utilized; system relies entirely on default UAM absorption and 7-hour max absorption hours.
analysis_steps.evidence: extended_carb_entries=0, meal_max_absorption_hours=7 h, min_5m_carbimpact=8 mg/dL/5 min.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of declared meal composition or extended carb logs.

analysis_steps.findings: Telemetry indicates that pure UAM reliance causes reactive peaks and late lows. Recommendations prioritize basal stability and optional meal logging before altering complex automation parameters.
analysis_steps.evidence: 86.0% TIR, 5.1% TBR, 0 explicit carb entries over 14 days.

strengths: High time-in-range of 86.0% across the 14-day monitoring period.
Excellent CGM data completeness and coverage at 98.7%.
Active closed-loop automation (SMB and UAM) successfully manages many unannounced glycemic excursions.
issues: Time below range of 5.1% exceeds the 4% safety threshold, with glucose extremes dipping to 41-42 mg/dL.
Afternoon post-prandial hyperglycemia reaches up to 32% time above range during peak hours.
Absence of manual carb entries forces closed-loop automation to react after absorption begins, causing insulin stacking and subsequent late hypoglycemia.

recommendations.title: Verify Overnight Basal Stability
recommendations.description: Overnight dips show 10% to 18.5% time below range between midnight and 02:00, indicating potential over-delivery or compounding IOB from afternoon corrections.

recommendations.title: Introduce Manual Meal Announcements
recommendations.description: Logging meals with explicit carb entries and modest preboluses can reduce post-prandial spikes and prevent aggressive reactive microbolusing.

profile_recommendation.rationale: Current profile settings and dynamic sensitivity provide reasonable overall control (86% TIR), but telemetry shows nocturnal dipping and post-prandial spikes due to unannounced meals rather than foundational basal defects.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Monitor overnight glucose trends and evaluate whether introducing manual carb entries improves post-prandial time above range before altering basal segments.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep current profile settings while initiating manual meal logging for verification.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Current rate of 0.6 U/h maintains overnight control, though nocturnal dipping requires careful monitoring of IOB and late corrections.
Morning basal segment is stable; no supporting evidence for change.
Basal rate supports early morning glucose requirements adequately.
Mid-day basal segment maintains stable fasting levels prior to afternoon meal periods.
Afternoon hyperglycemia is primarily driven by unannounced meals rather than a proven basal deficit.
Basal rate is appropriate for evening transition hours.
Basal rate maintains evening stability before night transitions.
Carb ratio segment is appropriate; lack of manual carb entries precludes empirical recalibration.
Morning CR segment operates effectively within closed-loop parameters.
Mid-day CR segment requires no adjustment without explicit meal data.
Afternoon CR segment is supported by dynamic sensitivity adjustments.
Evening CR segment maintains stable overnight entry conditions.
Flat ISF of 56 mg/dL/U is modulated by dynamic ISF (70%), which appropriately adapts to real-time resistance without profile changes.
Target of 90 mg/dL provides appropriate overnight glycemic control.
Target of 100 mg/dL accommodates daytime activity and meal transitions.
Target of 90 mg/dL ensures safe overnight settling.
10-hour DIA provides conservative insulin-on-board tracking, preventing premature aggressive corrections despite occasional IOB stacking.
Enabling both SMB and UAM is essential for managing unannounced meals given the current lack of manual carb entries.
smb_always_enabled=true supports automated delivery during unannounced rises, while keeping temp target SMB enabled maintains flexibility.
3-minute interval with 15-minute max SMB and 20-minute max UAM basal minutes provides well-controlled microbolus increments.
parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Safety ceilings of 12 U/h and 25 U provide appropriate broad operational safety bounds without restricting normal loop function.
Dynamic sensitivity at 70% effectively modulates ISF during resistance phases without requiring autosens target shifts.
Min carb impact of 8 mg/dL/5 min and 7-hour max absorption hours support robust UAM absorption tracking.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Introduce manual meal announcements with modest preboluses for known carbohydrate intake to reduce post-prandial spikes, allowing AAPS to manage tail absorption via UAM and SMB rather than reacting to sharp upward velocity.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Absence of manual meal records forces closed-loop automation to react after absorption begins, resulting in predictable post-prandial hyperglycemia followed by insulin stacking and late hypoglycemia.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log 3 to 5 meals with explicit carb entries and observe whether post-prandial time above range decreases without increasing nocturnal hypoglycemia risk.

exceptions.suggestion: Maintain current UAM-driven closed-loop automation without forced manual entries.
exceptions.rationale: Minor intake is efficiently captured by UAM without disrupting overall control.

exceptions.pattern: High-fat or complex meals with delayed absorption
exceptions.suggestion: Utilize declared extended carbohydrates (e-carbs) in AAPS.
exceptions.rationale: Prevents early insulin stacking and matches prolonged absorption tails.

implementation_steps: Step 1: Review data quality findings and confirm that CGM coverage and telemetry are stable.
Step 2: Monitor overnight glucose trends and verify that fasting basal rates remain appropriate before considering any basal adjustments.
Step 3: Begin logging manual meal announcements with modest preboluses for a subset of meals to evaluate impact on post-prandial spikes.
Step 4: Assess changes in time-in-range and time below range after introducing meal logging before making further automation adjustments.
education: Unannounced meals force closed-loop systems to react after glucose begins rising, which can lead to initial hyperglycemia and subsequent insulin stacking as the algorithm catches up.

Dynamic ISF and UAM work together to compensate for unannounced intake, but manual meal entry significantly improves post-prandial stability and reduces hypoglycemia risk from reactive insulin delivery.
